card.summary: H.R. 6575, titled the 'CommonGround for Affordable Health Care Act', amends the Internal Revenue Code and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. It extends and modifies enhanced health insurance premium tax credits for 2026, establishes fraud prevention guardrails and verification processes for Affordable Care Act exchanges and broker-assisted enrollments, extends the annual open enrollment period for plan year 2026, places new reporting and transparency requirements on pharmacy benefit managers in Medicare Part D, and sets expedited legislative procedures for future premium tax credit reform bills.

card.summary: H.R. 6501, titled the 'Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act', extends and modifies enhanced premium tax credits for health insurance under the Internal Revenue Code and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act through 2027. It establishes new guardrails to prevent fraud in health insurance exchanges by setting civil and criminal penalties for agents and brokers, adds requirements for agent-assisted enrollments and deceased individual removals, adjusts the annual open enrollment period for 2026, regulates pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) regarding transparency, reporting, and 100 percent rebate pass-throughs, and allows certain qualified exchange enrollees to establish and fund Health Savings Accounts (HSAs).

summary: The HOPE Act extends and modifies enhanced health insurance premium tax credits for taxable years 2026 and 2027, adjusts rules for the Affordable Care Act's health insurance exchanges, establishes new anti-fraud guardrails and civil or criminal penalties for agents and brokers, and extends the annual open enrollment period for plan year 2026.

affected_groups.effect: Receive an extension of enhanced premium tax credits through 2027, continued eligibility if household income is between 400 and 935 percent of the poverty line, clear notification of tax credit amounts prior to enrollment, and an extended 2026 open enrollment period.

Subject to stricter federal regulations, standards of conduct, mandatory registration, marketing material review, periodic audits, verification of consumer consent, delayed commissions, and severe civil and criminal penalties for fraud or negligence.
Tasked with implementing new verification processes, conducting Death Master File checks, performing periodic audits, sharing audit results, and notifying enrollees of changes or tax credit values.
affected_groups.group: Federal and State Governments and Exchanges

key_provisions: Extends enhanced premium tax credits through the end of 2027 and modifies the income percentage table for calculations.
Extends eligibility for the premium tax credit to taxpayers whose household income exceeds 400 percent of the poverty line, up to 935 percent, for taxable years 2026 and 2027.

Imposes new civil penalties ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 for negligence, and up to $200,000 for knowing violations, alongside criminal penalties (fines and up to 10 years imprisonment) for agents and brokers who provide false or fraudulent information.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish an enrollment verification process for federally operated exchanges, including documentation of consumer consent and delayed commission payments until inconsistencies are resolved.
Directs the Secretary to check the Death Master File quarterly to identify and remove deceased individuals from exchange qualified health plans.
Extends the annual open enrollment period for the 2026 plan year to run from November 1, 2025, through May 15, 2026.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The HOPE Act extends and modifies enhanced health insurance premium tax credits for taxable years 2026 and 2027, adjusts rules for the Affordable Care Act's health insurance exchanges, establishes new anti-fraud guardrails and civil or criminal penalties for agents and brokers, and extends the annual open enrollment period for plan year 2026.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal healthcare subsidies and regulatory oversight by continuing financial assistance expansions for middle- and lower-income health insurance purchasers through 2027 while substantially increasing penalties and bureaucratic guardrails to prevent fraudulent enrollments by agents and brokers.
